Rama's busy helping Min with a tricky case in Kaineng, so I thought I'd use the free time for some self-examination! Well, correction—I wanted to spend a week in Kourna researching a rare subspecies of beetle that collects water from fog. But I've been having problems sleeping again, so Taimi suggested taking some time for myself to analyze events that may have left a traumatic imprint on my psyche. Brains are magnificent and complicated organs!

Anyway, revisiting memories of the battle with Kralkatorrik has always been an acute challenge for me. But it's been a while since I evaluated everything that happened over that year. If I'm being honest, I could use an impartial perspective; the mind tends to wander when left to its own devices.

strings.en: You have gained %num1% faction with Balthazar!

Tribune Brimstone came by the tent to utilize our long-range comms devices a few afternoons ago. He tried for a moment or two, but he quickly erupted into growls of frustration—that charr has zero patience for technology. Snarled until I stood from my post to help—and by help, I just didn't want him to break anything—but this only seemed to irritate him further. I offered to take over the task for the sake of our equipment and my escalating blood pressure. He quickly surrendered.      
  
He was attempting to reach Rata Sum and the Black Citadel. I was hopeful for the former, but after a few promising signals, nothing. Attempting to reach the latter was optimistic at best.    
  
Rytlock muttered something about the "curse" on Isgarren before storming off to tend to more "important" matters. Could be, but I also wouldn't be surprised if the Inquest have managed to stifle any outgoing signals. Under these circumstances, all I can do is hypothesize.  
  
For now, we remain in the dark.

Fryst tried to chill his heart, but he couldn't stop the heat rising in his cheeks.

He was a good Svanir; he never questioned the teachings of his shaman. He always gave women the cold shoulder, knowing they were unworthy of Dragon.

But that was before Brenna. Brenna and her skilled sword hand and icy taunts. And her smile.

Burning questions exposed cracks in long-frozen ideals. What was this strange, molten feeling rising in the pit of his stomach? Was everything he'd been taught a lie? He was beginning to see that maybe he should rest.

I can sleep now, too. We can dream together beneath the ice. Let's rest, just for a while. Let's give up. All of us together, sleeping forever. I think I'll lie down.
